transcript:
Header: 2026-07-13 15:00 PDT | Duration: 62m
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Aditi Rao (Pinewell Head of Product), Marcus Li (Backend), Naomi Brooks (CTO), Evan Park (SRE)

[00:00] Liam: all right hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm Liam with Redwood Inference, we've got Sofia on the call to walk through the console and the runtime behavior, and Priya who'll handle next steps. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Aditi: good thanks, excited to see what we can do. we are trying to improve our storefront chat / product summary generator without blowing up costs.
[00:15] Naomi: and to add - we have a latency SLO: 200ms for short summarization requests under typical load, that's the ask from infra.
[00:22] Sofia: cool, good context. i'll start with a quick hosted API overview, then jump into the Console live, show model pinning, streaming, and then we'll demo some retry patterns. feel free to interrupt.
[00:34] [screen share starts] Sofia: So in the Console here you can see routes. Route -> model -> rollout policy. For Pinewell you could pin a low-latency variant for short responses and a higher-quality variant for long-form. We call these model variants, and you can set fallback to another variant if capacity's tight.
[00:52] Marcus: quick q - when you say fallback, is that automatic or policy-driven? we don't want surprises.
[00:57] Sofia: policy-driven—there's a routing policy; you can prioritize latency vs cost. we also show estimated token-cost per request in the console. The autoscaling + burst capacity is bounded so billing is predictable.
[01:12] Liam: to add, for POCs we usually recommend hosted to iterate quickly; Dedicated is for when you need dedicated GPU pools and absolute isolation. Private deployments for air-gapped/regulatory setups.
[01:25] Evan: any must-have security certifications?
[01:27] Priya: Redwood is SOC 2 compliant, we have ISO in process — we'll send the whitepaper and the KMS/HSM integration notes after the call.
[01:37] [01:37] Sofia: Switching to the API demo — we'll hit the chat endpoint. Note that streaming comes in chunks, and chunk size can be tuned client-side by buffer thresholds; server will flush partial tokens.
[01:50] [01:50] Sofia: I'm going to run a simple product-description prompt, short output so you see the streaming latency.
[01:57] [02:10] transcript note: audio glitch - 'buffer' heard as 'buffet' in transcript here
[02:15] [02:15] Sofia: (typing) POST /v1/chat/completions with messages: system/user, temperature 0.2, max_tokens 60, stream: true.
[02:25] [02:25] Sofia: you see first partial token at ~45ms, steady token flow thereafter. This is on our hosted region in us-west.
[02:35] Marcus: that seems fast; are you on A100s or H100s? what's the runtime?
[02:41] Sofia: we pick hardware per model profile; for small short-form generative loads we often route to smaller GPUs to optimize cost. The runtime uses KV cache and continuous batching, so cold-starts are low for repeated contexts.
[02:55] Naomi: So caching—is that per customer, and can we evict on demand?
[02:59] Sofia: yes per-customer prefix caching, evict via API, TTLs configurable. good for prompt-heavy patterns.
[03:08] [03:08] Liam: let's talk params — temperature controls randomness, top_p is nucleus sampling. For Pinewell for product bullets we usually recommend temperature 0.0-0.3, top_p 0.9, and enforce stop tokens to avoid trailing noise.
[03:25] Aditi: and max_tokens you'd tune by expected summary length?
[03:28] Sofia: exactly. also show you the Console 'simulate' panel — it overlays cost and latency estimates for param combos.
[03:36] [03:36] Sofia: now demo retry pattern — we'll simulate a transient 503 from the model shard. Best practice: client should retry idempotently for non-streaming requests, and for streaming we recommend resume semantics or fallback to a sync call with same prompt and a dedup token.
[03:55] Marcus: resume semantics? can you elaborate — we can't easily rehydrate partial responses on our side.
[03:59] Sofia: sure, two patterns: 1) server-side resume token—on reconnect you pass last-acknowledged token and server streams remaining; 2) if that's not doable, client retries with an idempotency key and Redwood will attempt de-dup—there are limits for streaming since partial output might be lost. we documented typical patterns in the retry playbook.
[04:20] [04:20] Aditi: i.e. what's the recommended backoff? exponential with jitter?
[04:24] Liam: yes exponential backoff with jitter, cap at say 10s for user-facing flows. For high-throughput background jobs you can be more aggressive but watch for duplicate side-effects.
[04:36] [04:36] Sofia: quick note on batching: for non-real-time batch jobs we suggest larger batch sizes and quantized models to reduce cost. Optimize (our recommendations engine) will look at latency distribution and suggest quantization profiles and batch sizes.
[04:50] Evan: Where does Optimize live — console or API?
[04:53] Sofia: Console -> Optimize tab. It gives suggestions, expected token cost delta, and rollout tooling to test quantized variants.
[04:59] [05:00] Naomi: question on data retention—do you keep customer prompts? for how long?
[05:04] Priya: by default Redwood stores logs for 30 days for troubleshooting; enterprise retention/archival is configurable and can be disabled for Private deployments. we'll include logging retention options in the security doc.
[05:18] [05:18] Sofia: jumping into a short live resilience test — i'll throttle the endpoint to force a 429/503 pattern so we can show recommended client backoff and fallback to a cheaper variant.
[05:30] [05:30] Sofia: (exec) -> client receives 429. we surface a Retry-After header. Client pause -> exponentially backoff -> either retry same model or route to a cheaper variant using the route policy.
[05:44] Marcus: does the console allow setting per-route fallback sequences? like first try small model, then medium, then heavyweight?
[05:51] Sofia: yep, you can chain fallback variants and also weight them for gradual rollouts. The tracing/log shows which fallback triggered and latency impact.
[06:04] Aditi: what's the SLA on hosted?
[06:07] Liam: Standard hosted SLA has 99.9 uptime for API, with latency targets based on model family. For mission-critical we recommend Dedicated with an SLA addendum.
[06:18] Naomi: And encryption — in flight and at rest?
[06:20] Priya: both — TLS in transit, and at rest you can integrate with your KMS for encryption of keys. We also support customer-managed keys for Private deployments.
[06:33] [06:33] Sofia: now a short walkthrough of code snippets — we'll show a streaming client in Node and a safe-retry wrapper. (reads snippet) use a per-request idempotency key for non-streaming, for streaming you should detect partials and attempt resume, otherwise fallback to an at-least-once re-request and dedupe downstream.
[06:54] Marcus: can you share that wrapper?
[06:56] Sofia: yes we'll include it in the follow-up repo link.
[06:59] [07:00] [minor crosstalk] Aditi: sorry just want to check, can we pin models per-team within our org?
[07:05] Liam: yes, RBAC supports per-route permissions; you can restrict who can change model pinning.
[07:12] Evan: what's the observability like for token-level cost breakdown?
[07:15] Sofia: Console shows token counts and cost per-token table, you can query logs for per-request tokens and export to your BI. We also expose traces for slow requests.
[07:28] [07:28] Sofia: quick performance note—if you need <200ms we often advise a smaller context window, model truncation, and aggressive caching of prefixes. Also consider model distillation / smaller variants.
[07:42] Naomi: would we be able to route EU traffic to eu-west region for residency?
[07:46] Liam: yes region routing available; for strict residency we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated in the target region.
[07:54] [07:54] Aditi: any gotchas we should prep for during a POC?
[07:58] Sofia: initial tokenization differences between model variants—if you compare outputs across variants, token counts/stop behaviors can vary. Also watch for tokenization-induced truncation for templates.
[08:12] [08:12] Marcus: about cost — do you have concrete numbers for small vs medium model per 1M tokens?
[08:16] Liam: we'll send the cost sheet; approximate numbers in the sheet reflect committed vs pay-as-you-go. Optimize provides simulated delta when you switch to a quantized variant.
[08:28] [08:28] Aditi: let's talk timeline — we're aiming to run a two-week pilot in August and decide by early Sept.
[08:34] Naomi: budget signoff in mid-August.
[08:36] Liam: great, we'll target a POC start in first week of August then. Sofia, can you coordinate tech bench with Marcus?
[08:43] Sofia: yes I'll draft a checklist — sample payloads, expected QPS, golden prompts for quality regression, and perf targets.
[08:52] [08:52] (brief pause)
[09:00] Priya: recap — action items: pricing & quickstart repo (Liam), benchmark checklist + sample payloads (Sofia), Pinewell to confirm POC team and traffic (Naomi). We'll also send SOC2 + KMS docs.
[09:15] Aditi: sounds good. one more question — competitors: we're also talking to OpenAI and Anthropic; curious how Redwood compares on cost transparency and rollout controls.
[09:26] Liam: our differentiator is runtime + ops: unified Console controls for model routing, built-in Optimize suggestions, and predictable cost controls for production. We'll include a one-pager.
[09:38] Naomi: ok thanks all.
[09:40] [09:40] Meeting ends, screen share off.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., 'buffet' for 'buffer'), speaker attribution sometimes generic.
